cards.back: A living thing that makes its own food. Green plants are producers.
cards.say: producer. A living thing that makes its own food. Green plants are producers.

cards.back: A living thing that gets energy by eating other living things.
cards.say: consumer. A living thing that gets energy by eating other living things.

cards.back: An animal that eats only plants.
cards.say: herbivore. An animal that eats only plants.

cards.back: An animal that eats only other animals.
cards.say: carnivore. An animal that eats only other animals.

cards.back: An animal that eats both plants and animals.
cards.say: omnivore. An animal that eats both plants and animals.

cards.back: An animal that hunts and eats other animals.
cards.say: predator. An animal that hunts and eats other animals.

cards.back: An animal that is hunted and eaten by another animal.
cards.say: prey. An animal that is hunted and eaten by another animal.

cards.back: A line of living things that shows what eats what, and how energy passes from one to the next.
cards.say: food chain. A line of living things that shows what eats what, and how energy passes from one to the next.

cards.front: What do the arrows in a food chain mean?
cards.back: They mean "is eaten by". They point from the food to the animal that eats it.
cards.say: What do the arrows in a food chain mean? They mean "is eaten by". They point from the food to the animal that eats it.

cards.front: Where does the energy in a food chain come from first?
cards.back: The Sun. Plants use sunlight to make food.
cards.say: Where does the energy in a food chain come from first? The Sun. Plants use sunlight to make food.

cards.back: The first consumer in a food chain. It eats a producer, so it is a herbivore.
cards.say: primary consumer. The first consumer in a food chain. It eats a producer, so it is a herbivore.

cards.back: A consumer that eats primary consumers.
cards.say: secondary consumer. A consumer that eats primary consumers.

cards.back: An animal at the end of a food chain that no other animal hunts.
cards.say: top predator. An animal at the end of a food chain that no other animal hunts.

cards.back: A living thing, such as a fungus or bacterium, that breaks down dead plants and animals and returns nutrients to the soil.
cards.say: decomposer. A living thing, such as a fungus or bacterium, that breaks down dead plants and animals and returns nutrients to the soil.

cards.back: An animal that feeds on the bodies of animals that are already dead. Vultures are scavengers.
cards.say: scavenger. An animal that feeds on the bodies of animals that are already dead. Vultures are scavengers.

cards.front: In grass, rabbit, fox, which is the producer?
cards.back: Grass. It makes its own food using sunlight.
cards.say: In grass, rabbit, fox, which is the producer? Grass. It makes its own food using sunlight.

cards.front: In grass, rabbit, fox, which is the predator?
cards.back: The fox. It hunts the rabbit, which is its prey.
cards.say: In grass, rabbit, fox, which is the predator? The fox. It hunts the rabbit, which is its prey.

cards.front: In grass, grasshopper, frog, snake, what is the snake's prey?
cards.back: The frog.
cards.say: In grass, grasshopper, frog, snake, what is the snake's prey? The frog.

cards.front: Why do most food chains start with a plant?
cards.back: Plants are the only living things in the chain that make their own food.
cards.say: Why do most food chains start with a plant? Plants are the only living things in the chain that make their own food.

cards.front: What may happen to rabbit numbers if all the foxes disappear?
cards.back: They may rise at first, because fewer rabbits are eaten. Then they may eat too much grass.
cards.say: What may happen to rabbit numbers if all the foxes disappear? They may rise at first, because fewer rabbits are eaten. Then they may eat too much grass.

cards.front: What may happen to foxes if all the rabbits disappear?
cards.back: They have less food, so some may starve or move away to find food.
cards.say: What may happen to foxes if all the rabbits disappear? They have less food, so some may starve or move away to find food.

cards.front: Is a human a producer or a consumer?
cards.back: A consumer. Humans eat plants and animals, so they are omnivores.
cards.say: Is a human a producer or a consumer? A consumer. Humans eat plants and animals, so they are omnivores.

cards.front: Why do food chains usually have only four or five links?
cards.back: Some energy is lost at every step, so there is not enough left to support more links.
cards.say: Why do food chains usually have only four or five links? Some energy is lost at every step, so there is not enough left to support more links.
